findings.summary: First execution of the HARDENED distillation-gated pruning policy deleted ZERO runs (deleted=0 kept=55 unarchived=0 failed=0). Direct behavioral contrast with v1 execution of 2026-08-25T17:57Z (run 32880942022: deleted=102 kept=54): the new gate requires evidence/run-memory/runs/<id>.json to exist AND carry distillation_complete=true AND safe_to_prune=true before any completed, unprotected run may be deleted. Protection layers observed active: non-completed runs protected; runs whose id appears in cycle/* branch names or other durable refs protected via PROTECT map; latest KEEP_LATEST_PER_WORKFLOW=3 per workflow protected; archived-but-not-prune-safe runs explicitly kept ('Keeping archived-but-protected run ... safe=false distilled=false' branch present in script). No provenance incident occurred in this run.

Observability gap in the hardened guard: the summary line reports kept=55 but NO per-run 'Keeping ...' decision lines were emitted at runtime - every keep came from silent continue paths (non-completed status or PROTECT-map membership), so the log alone cannot show WHY each specific run was retained. Auditability of protection decisions currently rests on script source + rerun rather than on the execution log. Suggested fix: emit one line per kept run with its protection reason class.

SPECIAL RECOVERY check performed during distillation: recovery-trigger run 32880942022 was NOT among the supplied bundles for this batch; its prior recovery state was verified instead of rebuilt. DELETED_RUNS_RECOVERY.json satisfies the dual-key invariant (deleted_run_count == total_deleted_runs == 102), loss_assessment_counts sum to 102 (98 NONE_MATERIAL / 0 LOW / 4 UNKNOWN / 0 MATERIAL_RISK), all 102 deleted ids match the 102 tombstone files under evidence/run-memory/deleted/, and hygiene #2 itself deleted nothing - therefore no new tombstones are required and no recovery action was taken.

research_opportunities: Retention-policy tuning now has a working feedback loop: as curator passes set safe_to_prune=true on clean orchestration no-ops, subsequent hygiene executions will start deleting them automatically. The first such deletion batch should be spot-audited against INDEX.md claims before trusting the end-to-end loop.

It also remains inside the latest-3-per-workflow retention window anyway. Re-evaluate for prune-safety once several clean gated executions have accumulated.
